name: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension
grip: Overhand pronated grip with hands approximately shoulder-width apart (or slightly narrower) on the barbell.
description: Lower a barbell toward the forehead or crown of the head by bending the elbows while lying supine on a flat bench, then extend the elbows to isolate all three heads of the triceps brachii.
setup: Lie flat on a bench with your head near the end of the pad and feet firmly planted on the floor.
Hold a barbell with an overhand grip, hands spaced 6 to 10 inches apart (shoulder-width or slightly narrower).
Extend your arms straight up over your chest or angled slightly backward toward your head (~10-15 degrees) to keep continuous tension on the triceps.
instructions: Lower the barbell slowly by bending your elbows, allowing the bar to descend toward your forehead or just past the crown of your head.
Keep your upper arms stationary and elbows tucked in without flaring outward excessively.
Pause briefly just above the forehead/crown without letting the bar touch the head or rest.
Extend your elbows smoothly by contracting your triceps to press the bar back up to the starting position.
cues: Keep elbows tucked and pointing toward the ceiling.
Control the negative descent to the forehead.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows outward, transforming the movement into a close-grip press.
Swinging the upper arms forward and back to use shoulder momentum.
Descending too fast with heavy loads, risking impact with the head.

logging.example: Barbell loaded to 30 kg: record 30 kg total barbell mass.
logging.note: Record total mass of barbell plus all loaded plates. Often performed with an EZ-curl bar; note bar type if applicable.

variantNote: Supine free-weight triceps extension isolating elbow extension. Angling the upper arms slightly backward maintains tension on the triceps long head even at the top of the movement.
